st-01: With the throat consecrated by Ganga from the forest of jata, a tall snake-garland hanging, Shiva danced the fierce tandava to the damaru’s damat — may He grant auspiciousness.
st-02: Ganga whirls in the cauldron of jata; the brow-fire blazes; the young moon rests on His crest — may my love rest there every moment.
st-03: Friend of Parvati’s play, whose mind delights to the horizon, whose glance of grace checks calamity — may the mind sport in that sky-clad One.
st-04: Jewel-light from tawny snake-hoods paints the quarters; elephant-hide as upper cloth — may the mind bear wonder in the Lord of beings.
st-05: His footstool grey with flower-dust of Indra and the gods; jata bound with the serpent-king’s garland — may the moon-crested One grant lasting fortune.
st-06: Sparks from the brow-fire drank Kama’s five arrows; the lord of gods bows; nectar-rayed crest — may that matted crown be our fortune.
st-07: On the terrible brow-plate fire made Kama an offering; the sole artist of Parvati’s painted marks — may my love rest on the Three-eyed.
st-08: Neck bound in new-cloud dark of the new-moon night; bearer of Ganga and elephant-hide, friend of the moon — may the world’s bearer grant fortune.
st-09: I worship Him whose throat is the dark of a full blue lotus — cutter of Kama, of the Triple City, of becoming, of the sacrifice, of the elephant, of Andhaka, of Death.
st-10: Bee at the overflowing sweetness of Uma’s cluster of auspicious arts — I worship the Ender of Kama, of the cities, of becoming, of the rite, of the elephant, of Andhaka, of Death.
st-11: Victory to Shiva — snake-breath from sky-play fans the brow-fire; the fierce tandava steps to the high auspicious mridanga’s dhimid-dhimid.
st-12: When shall I worship Sadashiva with even regard — pebble or painted couch, snake or pearl, gem or clod, friend or foe, grass or lotus, subject or Indra?
st-13: When, dwelling in a Ganga-grove, rid of ill thought, hands on the head, ash on the brow, uttering the mantra Shiva — shall I be at ease?
st-14: Reading, remembering, speaking this highest hymn daily, a person is continually purified; devotion to Hari and Guru comes swiftly — thought of Shankara undoes the body’s delusion.
st-15: Who recites this ten-faced song at the close of puja in pradosha — Shambhu grants him stable, well-faced Lakshmi with chariot, elephant and horse.
